item.title: Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis
item.description: By Udeme Akpan Power sector experts have called for accelerated deployment of renewable energy and microgrids to address Nigeria’s persistent electricity supply challenges and reduce dependence on the national grid. Speaking in separate interviews with Vanguard at the recently concluded Nigeria Energy Summit in Lagos, they said decentralised power solutions would improve electricity access, particularly for businesses and rural communities. Product Manager, DEIF, Anshul Alankar, said: “The reality is that renewable energy is the in-thing, and government policy also supports it. It is important to latch on to it as early as possible, especially for the commercial sector and even for individual users. “The grid system is not able to provide all the electricity and power needed by Nigerians and Africans to maintain sustainable energy. “Nigeria has surplus solar energy, and microgrids will help because you don’t need huge infrastructure to bring power across the country. “Microgrids are a more efficient way of handling local and rural areas. You can create your own grid, minimise fuel consumption and maximise the sun, which is free.” On the growing demand for decentralised energy, he said: “We see that the need of the market is around microgrids and fuel efficiency. We provide solutions that enable batteries to work more efficiently and solar panels to be maximised.” Also speaking, Executive Director, Delmira Power Solutions, Dr. Moriam Jagun, said the company was bringing advanced power management solutions into Nigeria. She said its technologies “coordinate, protect and monitor energy, making sure that energy is efficiently generated and delivered, both for land and marine.” Sales Head, Engineering, Delmira Power Solutions, Engr. Nmecha Chizinum Ayodele, said: “Our country has come to the point of further expansion in renewable energy, from household to grid levels.” He added: “DEIF solutions can remotely monitor, automate and synchronise different power sources to provide all-round power for industries and homes, thereby reducing the cost of energy.” The post Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US Midterm: Democrats Retake Senate In Major Blow Against Trump’s Republican
item.description: Democrats won full control of the US Congress in a sweeping midterm rout Tuesday with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times: “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats.” But minutes later on social media, the 80-year-old signaled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.” The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of the party’s inroads into Republican strongholds. The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters. Texas was a political bombshell. Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office. Democrats also protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. Republicans had held a 53-47 Senate majority. The six-seat Democratic gain proved sufficient for networks to project a takeover despite some races remaining unresolved. Supporters of Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico cheer after he won the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Republican Heartland Democrats also captured the House after flipping Republican-held districts in states stretching from Pennsylvania and New Jersey to Kentucky, Arizona and North Carolina. Some victories came in territory Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, despite Republican attempts to shore up House seats by redrawing electoral boundaries. One bellwether was Indiana, where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points. item.title: Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness — Feese
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Nigeria Economic Summit Group has warned that high production costs, unreliable electricity and poor logistics infrastructure are undermining Nigeria’s industrial competitiveness, calling for a council within the Presidency to coordinate industrialisation policies. Co-facilitator of the NESG, Lumun Feese, said Nigeria needed a coordinated approach to industrial development to address structural challenges and enable local manufacturers to compete effectively in African markets. She spoke at a breakout session on building an integrated industrial ecosystem during the 32nd Nigeria Economic Summit on Tuesday in Abuja. Feese said Nigeria had dropped from eighth to 14th position on the African Development Bank’s Africa Industrialisation Index, although she noted that the methodology had changed and more countries had been included in the latest ranking. She said, “We are not maximising our potential and our large economy. “How do we go and compete in South Africa when our cost of production is so high? Power, logistics and so on and so forth.” She added that Nigeria needed to move beyond its domestic market and develop the capacity to supply other African countries. Feese said the proposed industrialisation, competitiveness and regional integration council would provide a central coordinating platform within the Presidency to align government policies, improve implementation of the National Industrial Policy and strengthen private-sector participation. She said Nigerian businesses needed reliable power, efficient transportation systems and lower production costs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area, which offers access to a wider continental market. Feese said the recommendations followed consultations on mining, the blue economy, power, oil and gas, and industrial competitiveness. She urged businesses and other stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the NESG’s Industrial Policy Commission, saying coordinated policies and consistent implementation were necessary to achieve measurable industrial growth. item.title: ADC vows to proceed with Sokoto campaign despite intimidation
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has vowed to proceed with its scheduled campaign in Sokoto State despite what it described as attempts by the state government to intimidate the opposition and obstruct its political activities. The party also warned that Governor Ahmed Aliyu would be held responsible if any violence was directed at opposition members or supporters in the state. The ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, stated this in a statement issued on Tuesday, accusing the Sokoto State Government of undermining democratic rights and deliberately frustrating the party’s activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Abdullahi said the party would not be deterred by the alleged intimidation, insisting that no governor had the authority to prevent any political party from campaigning or presenting its candidates to voters. “The Sokoto State Government must understand that governing a state does not confer ownership. Public office is a temporary mandate from the people, not a licence to suppress political competition,” the statement read. “No governor has the power to decide which party can campaign, which candidate can speak, or which political choices the people of Sokoto are allowed to consider.” The ADC spokesperson called on the state government to immediately stop what he described as efforts to frustrate its lawful political activities and guarantee a level playing field for all political parties. He also reminded security agencies and other public institutions that their responsibility was to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, rather than the political interests of the ruling party. Abdullahi warned that public officials who abused their authority to obstruct lawful political activities would face the legal consequences of their actions. “Let there be no misunderstanding. The ADC will campaign in Sokoto State. We will not be intimidated, obstructed or pushed out of any part of Nigeria simply because those in power are afraid of political competition,” he said. He maintained that democratic participation was a constitutional right and not a privilege to be granted by elected public officials. The ADC spokesperson further accused the ruling party of displaying intolerance towards opposition activities, challenging it to submit itself to an open contest if it believed it had performed well in government. item.title: Petrol hits N1,370/litre as depot prices rise
item.description: By Udeme Akpan The pump price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol, has risen to N1,370 per litre in Lagos, following fresh increases in depot prices across major supply locations. Checks by Vanguard on Tuesday showed that MRS and NNPC filling stations sold petrol at N1,360 per litre, while Mobil sold at N1,349. Some independent marketers sold at between N1,365 and N1,370, depending on location. The increase followed sharp movements in depot prices, particularly in Lagos, where A.A. Rano raised its PMS price by N75 to N1,295 per litre, while African Terminal, Aiteo and Integrated increased their prices to about N1,300. NIPCO also raised its price by N55 to N1,305, while Dangote’s price edged up by N3 to N1,303. MRS retained its depot price at N1,310. In Port Harcourt, Matrix increased its PMS price by N15 to N1,300 per litre, while Bulk Strategic, Masters and T.S.L remained at N1,300. Warri also recorded increases, with A.Y.M. Shafa and Matrix raising their prices by N17 each to N1,300, while Parker moved up by N15 to the same level. Calabar recorded higher PMS prices, with Fynefield and Northwest at N1,360 per litre. Meanwhile, Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel, recorded mixed movements. In Lagos, WOSBAB cut its AGO price by N21 to N1,809 per litre, while Bulk Strategic reduced its price by N15 to N1,835. Rain Oil and Dangote also reduced their prices to N1,850 and N1,823 respectively. In Warri, Matrix and Rain Oil cut their AGO prices by N5 each to N1,835 per litre, while Edo Refinery, NIPCO and Prudent retained theirs at N1,840. The latest figures point to continued volatility in the downstream market as changes in depot prices filter through to retail outlets. “To safeguard port integrity and vessel safety, all maritime operators, terminal users, and personnel must utilise authorised reporting protocols immediately upon detecting any security incident or anomaly,” the agency stated. item.title: NIMASA threatens sanctions over missing marine incident reports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has threatened sanctions against Port Facility Security Officers (PFSOs) who fail to properly report marine security incidents, warning that bypassing approved reporting channels constitutes a breach of international port security rules. The warning followed concerns that incident reports from port facilities were being sent to individual NIMASA officials instead of the agency’s designated International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Unit. In a notice signed by Mudi Isa, Head, ISPS Code Unit, the agency directed all PFSOs to route incident reports through the approved ISPS Unit email address. The notice, titled “Non-Receipt of Incident Reports/Submission to Approved ISPS Unit,” said: “It has come to our attention that the Unit is currently not receiving your incident report emails, which poses a significant risk.” NIMASA warned that the failure to use the prescribed channel could have serious implications for maritime security. “Failure to report security incidents to the correct channels constitutes a breach of ISPS compliance,” it stated. The agency specifically directed port facility security personnel to stop sending or copying reports to individual NIMASA staff emails unless expressly authorised. “Do not copy or send reports to individual staff emails unless explicitly authorised,” the notice stated. NIMASA also directed PFSOs to confirm receipt of every incident report and contact the ISPS Unit immediately if no acknowledgement was received within 24 hours. “If you do not receive an acknowledgment from the ISPS Unit within 24hrs of submission, contact the Unit immediately via phone,” it said. The agency further advised operators who were unsure of the approved reporting directory to contact the ISPS Unit for verification before submitting their reports. NIMASA said the directive was aimed at ensuring that security incidents and anomalies are captured promptly and handled through a coordinated response mechanism. item.title: Nigeria’s exports record 25% increase in 2yrs — NPA
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Nigeria’s exports have increased by 25 per cent in the last two years, driven by Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port terminal operators, the Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, has said. Speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH), Dantsoho said the growth covered both oil and non-oil exports. “For us in Nigeria, the most important thing is that we are seeing growth as a result of this policy that we are taking. Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. “These are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In manufacturing and agriculture, raw materials like cocoa and cashew, volumes have increased, and that is to the credit of the partnership between ourselves and the major terminal operators, APM Terminals,” he said. He attributed the improvement to Export Processing Terminals established by the NPA. “We have got about four of those in Nigeria where we collaborate with the terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other agencies that have a stake, so that everything regarding the processing of cargo for export is done locally,” he stated. On the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), Dantsoho said: “Nigeria’s economy is very strong now because of our president’s reforms, which everyone can testify is attracting investors to the country.” He added that port reforms had improved operational efficiency and increased revenue. “We have experienced a lot of increase in volumes and revenue that has been generated by the ports across Nigeria. As a matter of fact, the efficiency in the ports in Nigeria is far better now than those of other West African countries,” he said. Dantsoho also disclosed that the Federal Government was investing $1 billion in expanding and modernising Apapa Port, with private-sector partnerships supporting infrastructure and technology development. item.title: US Midterms: Trump accepts midterm results, pledges to work with Democrats
item.description: United States President Donald Trump has said he is prepared to accept the outcome of the country’s midterm elections and work with Democrats, as results showed the opposition party heading towards control of both chambers of Congress. Trump made the remarks on Tuesday night during a telephone interview with The New York Times, as he monitored election results at the White House. “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” he said. “We’ll probably work something out.” The President’s comments came amid major Republican losses, with Democrats making significant gains in closely contested races and threatening Republican control of Congress. Trump attributed his party’s poor performance partly to his absence from the ballot, suggesting that his participation could have changed the outcome. He also defended his decision to launch a war against Iran, describing it as a “very wise decision”. The President further said he had no regrets about endorsing Republican candidates, including South Carolina Senator Darline Graham and Texas Attorney-General Ken Paxton, who both lost their Senate bids. Speaking shortly before 10:30pm on Tuesday, Trump said he was following the election results during the interview. “I’m just looking at these results as I’m talking,” he said. Reacting to Graham’s defeat, he added: “I see that Darline lost. Wow, that’s amazing. How do you think Lindsey would have done if he ran?” He was referring to Senator Lindsey Graham, who reportedly died in July. Democrats were on course to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate as results continued to emerge, PUNCH Online had reported on Wednesday. A Democratic takeover of Congress would significantly alter the balance of political power in Washington, potentially subjecting Trump’s administration to increased congressional scrutiny and making it more difficult for the President to advance his legislative agenda during the remaining two years of his term. item.title: ADC accuses Sokoto govt of intimidation, demands reopening of campaign office
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Sokoto State Government of using the police to intimidate opposition politicians and frustrate its political activities, following the sealing of its state campaign office in Sokoto. The party demanded the immediate reopening of the premises, describing the action as illegal and an infringement on its constitutional rights ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the ADC said its campaign office along Ahmadu Bello Way in Sokoto metropolis was sealed on Tuesday, November 3, by officers of the Sokoto State Police Command allegedly acting on the orders of the state government. The development occurred barely hours before the commencement of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in the state, with the proposed campaign venue reportedly remaining locked. The statement was signed by Yusuf Suleiman, also known as Dan Amar Sokoto, Deputy Director-General of Administration of the Atiku Abubakar ADC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, and made available to journalists. The party alleged that the premises were sealed without a court order, prior notice or any lawful explanation from the authorities. It described the action as “illegal, unconstitutional and reckless”, arguing that it violated its rights to freedom of association, peaceful assembly and political participation. The ADC also cited Section 95 of the Electoral Act 2026, arguing that the action undermined the legal protections available to registered political parties to organise and conduct their activities without unlawful interference. The party further linked the development to what it described as a pattern of political intimidation in the state, recalling an alleged attack on its governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, at Sultan Sadiq Abubakar International Airport four days earlier. It dismissed suggestions that the authorities might not have known who occupied the building, insisting that the party had operated openly from the premises for more than eight years. “The claim that the authorities do not know who occupies the building is not credible. The ADC has operated openly from those premises for more than eight years,” the statement said. The party argued that any genuine inquiry into the ownership or occupation of the property should have been made through a formal letter rather than the deployment of armed police officers to seal its premises. It also alleged that the state government was concerned about the growing support for the ADC and its candidates, accusing it of responding to political competition with force rather than democratic engagement. “We reject this conduct in its entirety. We will pursue every legitimate and lawful remedy available to us to reopen our office and to protect our members, our supporters and our property in Sokoto,” it stated. item.title: LG reinforces leadership in refrigerator market with Brandcom award
item.description: LG Electronics has strengthened its position in Nigeria’s home appliance market following the recognition of its MoodUP Refrigerator at the BRANDCOM awards 2026 in Lagos. The award recognises the refrigerator’s distinctive design and smart features, including customisable LED door panels and smart connectivity, which allow users to personalise their kitchen experience. Beyond its aesthetics, LG’s refrigerator range addresses practical household needs such as food preservation, energy efficiency and durability, which remain important considerations for Nigerian consumers. The company offers top-freezer, bottom-freezer, side-by-side and premium refrigerator models designed to accommodate different household sizes and lifestyles. One of its products, the GN-F452PFAQ Top Freezer Refrigerator, features FRESH Converter+ technology, which allows users to adjust temperature settings to suit different food types and maintain optimal freshness. It also comes with an automatic ice maker for added convenience. Selected LG refrigerator models are equipped with Smart Inverter Compressor , LINEARCooling and DoorCooling+ technologies, designed to improve energy efficiency, provide consistent cooling and preserve food freshness for longer. These features are particularly relevant to households seeking reliable refrigeration, lower energy consumption and dependable appliance performance. The recognition at the BRANDCOM Awards further highlights LG’s presence in Nigeria’s competitive refrigerator market. item.title: REFORMS: Oil output has grown by 600,000bpd since PIA — NNPC
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Nigeria’s crude oil production has increased by 600,000 barrels per day (bpd), from about 1.2 million bpd to 1.8 million bpd, following the implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) and reforms in the oil and gas sector, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has said. Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr Bashir Bayo Ojulari, disclosed this yesterday at the 2026 Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition and Conference (ADIPEC) in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Speaking at an Energy Talk titled, “Nigeria’s Reform Agenda: Competing for Energy Capital,” Ojulari attributed the production increase to the implementation of the PIA 2021, improved investment climate, better investment decisions and stronger collaboration between NNPC and its partners. He said the company was working towards achieving Nigeria’s two million bpd production ambition by 2027 through improved maintenance of existing infrastructure, protection of base production, increased output from producing assets and execution of new projects. “The figure of 1.8 million barrels per day is a stage in a journey towards our objective. We are concentrating on the basics, which are maintaining our infrastructure, protecting base operations and executing the projects that will take production higher,” he said. On domestic energy supply, the NNPC boss said the removal of petrol subsidy had been accompanied by a major compressed natural gas (CNG) programme, with more than 400 conversion centres established across the country. He added that over 1,000 trucks used in transporting petroleum products had also been converted to run on CNG. Ojulari disclosed that the Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) gas pipeline was completed in August 2026, while the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) pipeline was expected to deliver gas to Abuja before the end of the year to support power generation, data centres and industrial hubs. On gas development, he said NNPC was targeting national production of 10 billion standard cubic feet per day (Bscf/d) by 2027 and 12 Bscf/d by 2030, supported by the development of domestic and international markets. He also said the countries involved in the Nigeria-Morocco Gas Pipeline had aligned and executed the necessary agreements, while Nigeria, Algeria and Niger had reached alignment on the development of the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline. On investment, Ojulari cited major projects, including TotalEnergies’ Ubeta, Shell’s Bonga South-West and Eni’s Zabazaba developments, noting that commercial agreements covering about $20 billion in investments had been concluded. He added that NNPC was building new relationships with international partners, including the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) and Chinese investors in Nigeria’s refineries, while working with global oilfield service companies to expand capacity in the country. item.title: US Midterms: Democrats take control of US Congress as voters reject Trump’s Republicans
item.description: Democrats have taken control of both chambers of the United States Congress in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, dealing a major political setback to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. The victory marks a significant shift in the balance of power in Washington, giving Democrats control of the House of Representatives and the Senate for the remaining two years of Trump’s presidency. According to the BBC, Democrats had secured a majority in the House of Representatives as of Wednesday, although vote counting was continuing in several states. The figures available at the time of filing this report showed Democrats with 194 seats in the House against 115 for Republicans, while in the Senate, Democrats had secured 52 seats against 40 for Republicans. The Democratic Party also recorded major upsets in several closely contested Senate races, winning Republican-held seats in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, while retaining Democratic seats in Georgia and New Hampshire. In Texas, Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton, becoming the first Democrat to win a Senate seat in the state since 1988. In South Carolina, Democrat Annie Andrews defeated Republican Darline Graham, becoming the first woman elected to the US Senate from the state and the first Democrat to win a Senate seat there in more than two decades. Democrat Roy Cooper also defeated Republican Michael Whatley in North Carolina, while Sherrod Brown defeated Republican incumbent Jon Husted to win the Ohio Senate race. The results represent a major reversal of political fortunes for Republicans, whose control of Congress had given Trump’s administration considerable legislative advantage. The midterm elections, held on Tuesday, November 3, determine the composition of the United States Congress, comprising the 435-member House of Representatives and the 100-member Senate. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats were contested. The Democratic takeover is expected to intensify congressional scrutiny of Trump’s administration, with the opposition party gaining control of key committees and greater powers to investigate government policies and decisions. The BBC reported that Democratic control of the House could significantly constrain what Trump could achieve during the remaining two years of his presidency. Democrats could launch investigations into the president and his family, as well as controversial decisions and policies of his administration. Reacting to the Republican losses, Trump sought to distance himself from the outcome, arguing that his absence from the ballot contributed to the party’s poor performance. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” he wrote on his Truth Social platform. item.title: NESG: Economic growth must deliver jobs, higher incomes
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe Chairman of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG), Mr. Omoboyede Olusanya, has called for a shift from measuring Nigeria’s economic progress by headline growth figures to delivering tangible improvements in jobs, incomes, productivity and living standards. Olusanya made the call at the closing of the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES#32) in Abuja, saying: “Growth that delivers is growth whose impact is strongly felt. “It means farmers earn more because their productivity has improved; manufacturers produce at lower cost; graduates find decent jobs; businesses access affordable financing; and children receive the nutrition and healthcare they need to thrive.” Introducing “Growth that Delivers” as the guiding principle of his tenure as NESG chairman, he said: “While recent reforms have helped restore macroeconomic stability, stability is only the starting point. “Bridging the distance between macroeconomic stability and accelerated growth, and between accelerated growth and improved lives and livelihoods, is the task before us all.” Outlining his priorities, Olusanya pledged to make accountability a central feature of the organisation’s engagement with government and other stakeholders. “We will ensure that every priority commitment from this Summit has a designated owner, a timeline and measurable indicators of success, building on the NES Accountability Framework and publishing progress ahead of NES#33,” he stated. On evidence-driven policy, he said: “We will strengthen our research and policy intelligence to produce rigorous, practical and costed recommendations linked to the National Development Plan 2026–2030.” On investment mobilisation, he pledged that the NESG would work with government, financial institutions and development partners to “turn policy ideas into bankable projects and mobilise capital into agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure, technology, entrepreneurship and skills.” He also promised to expand economic opportunities across all regions and states, with greater attention to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and the informal economy. On institutional sustainability, he said the NESG would broaden its membership, increase the participation of women and young people, protect its independence and strengthen its sustainability for future generations. Calling for collective action, Olusanya urged governments at all levels to “sustain and improve reforms, reduce the costs of power, logistics and doing business, and maintain predictable policies backed by clear, measurable commitments.” He challenged private-sector leaders to “invest, innovate, develop workforce skills, pay fairly and create productive jobs.” He also urged young Nigerians to “build enterprises, acquire relevant skills and hold institutions accountable,” while calling on civil society to monitor commitments and amplify the voices of underserved communities. item.title: Naira rises, now N1,374/$ in parallel market
item.description: …As interbank turnover rises 445% By Elizabeth Adegbesan The Naira yesterday appreciated to N1,374 per dollar from N1,377 in the parallel market on Monday. But the naira depreciated to N1,347.75 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the official market rose slightly to N1,347.75 per dollar from N1,346.01 per dollar on Monday, indicating N1.74 depreciation for the naira. Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N26.25 per dollar from N30.99 per dollar on Monday. The value of interbank turnover in NFEM increased sharply by 445.6 percent to $118.95 billion from $21.8 billion on Monday. item.title: Police rescue Nigerian woman sold for N770,000 in Mali
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has rescued a 21-year-old Nigerian woman trafficked to Mali and forced into prostitution, arresting three suspected members of an international human trafficking syndicate. The operation was carried out by operatives of the Special Tactical Squad, Force Intelligence Department (STS-FID), following an intelligence-led investigation into the trafficking network. The development was disclosed during a press briefing by ACP Victor Ogbeide Godfrey, who coordinated the operation. He said the suspects were arrested between October 1 and 27, 2026. The suspects were identified as Daniel Aondofa, 26; Orgba Solomon, 28, also known as Terry; and ThankGod Ocho, 25. All three are indigenes of Benue State, while Solomon was identified as the alleged leader of the syndicate. The police said the victim, Patience Darius, from Akwanga, Nasarawa State, was lured by Solomon with promises of lucrative employment opportunities abroad. According to the police, she was taken to Lagos on September 26 before being moved through illegal border routes into the Benin Republic and subsequently transported to gold-mining camps in Mali, where women were allegedly forced into prostitution. Solomon reportedly confiscated her mobile phone and travel documents before taking her out of Nigeria, cutting off communication with her family and friends. Upon arrival in Mali, she was allegedly handed over to two individuals identified as Mohammed and Marian, also known as Riana, before being sold for 420,000 CFA francs, equivalent to approximately N770,000. Recounting her ordeal, the victim said she was severely beaten for refusing to engage in prostitution and subsequently taken to a shrine, where she was forced to take a blood oath. The police report quoted her as saying that when she refused to engage in prostitution, she was “beaten blue and black” and taken to a shrine, where she was forced to take a blood oath before being compelled into prostitution. The Force said the investigation began after the victim’s sister lodged a complaint, prompting operatives to deploy digital intelligence to track the trafficking network. It said Solomon was arrested after returning to Nigeria to recruit more women for trafficking to Senegal and Mali, while the two other suspects were also apprehended. The suspects reportedly confessed to their involvement in the crime and provided information that facilitated the victim’s rescue from Mali. The police further disclosed that Darius alleged that about 42 Nigerian women were being held in a makeshift camp within a gold-mining settlement in Mali, where they were subjected to forced prostitution and slave-like conditions. According to the victim, the women were kept under strict surveillance, making escape almost impossible. item.title: ADC’s struggle to campaign
item.description: There was an air of uncertainty on Tuesday over whether the flag-off of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign in Sokoto State scheduled for Wednesday (today) would be held as planned. Daily Trust gathered that, as of Tuesday evening, the party was still struggling to secure a venue for the event, mobilise supporters, and make other basic logistical arrangements for the rally. Our correspondents report that the event was initially scheduled for Saturday, October 31, but was shifted to Wednesday due to the alleged takeover of hotel bookings by the state government, which has denied the claim. It was learnt that due to problems of logistics, some ADC leaders in the state offered their homes and guest houses to accommodate party leaders and other dignitaries arriving for the party’s presidential campaign flag-off. Some party leaders confirmed this in separate interviews with our correspondents, saying they resorted to providing private accommodation after failing to secure hotel rooms for their guests. Spokesman for the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Aminu Abubakar, said the party was yet to secure hotel accommodation, prompting members to volunteer their residences and guest houses. “Some of them have offered their homes, while others have provided their guest houses to accommodate our visitors. That is where we are putting them up,” he said. Another party chieftain, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said some prominent party leaders had already arrived in Sokoto ahead of the event. He said they include the party’s National Secretary and former Osun State Governor, Rauf Aregbesola; Senator Dino Melaye; and the party’s governorship candidate in Kaduna State, Isa Ashiru Kudan. The source added that more party leaders and dignitaries were expected to arrive Tuesday night or early Wednesday. However, the party was yet to officially announce the exact venue of the rally as of the time of filing this report. Supporters of the ADC in Sokoto yesterday An unverified source claimed that the event would take place at the Trade Fair Complex, while another source said it would be held at the party’s office premises along Ahmadu Bello Way, which was recently sealed by the state government. A source familiar with the arrangement alleged that the party had been asked to pay N20 million for the use of the Trade Fair Complex. According to the source, the party had agreed to the payment and requested the account details to enable it to transfer the money, but the details had yet to be provided. Director-General of the ADC Governorship Campaign Council, Bello Muhammad Goronyo, when contacted for clarification on the arrival of party leaders and the venue of the event declined to comment, saying he was not aware of the arrival of the guests or where the presidential campaign flag-off would take place. item.title: Experts seek soil-based fertiliser recommendations to improve yields
item.description: By Cynthia Alo Agricultural experts have called for a shift from one-size-fits-all fertiliser recommendations to soil-based application, warning that farmers may be wasting money on nutrients their crops do not need. They said differences in soil conditions and crop requirements meant that applying the same fertiliser rates across farming locations could result in poor nutrient use, higher production costs and lower productivity. The experts spoke at the 2026 Nigeria Fertiliser Summit on Phosphorus and Food Security, organised by the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), Obafemi Awolowo University and the Fertilizer Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN), with the Fertilizer and Inputs Support Services Department of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security as co-convener in Abuja. Findings presented at the summit by the Regional Hub for Fertilizer and Soil Health for West Africa and the Sahel showed that phosphorus requirements for maize and rice in northern Nigeria ranged from zero to more than 60 kilogrammes of phosphorus pentoxide per hectare, depending on soil conditions. Phosphorus is an essential plant nutrient that supports root development, crop growth and grain formation. However, its availability to crops varies with soil properties and farming conditions. A soil scientist and modelling expert at IAR&T, Prof. Vincent Aduramigba-Modupe, said improving agricultural productivity required more than increasing fertiliser application. “Improving crop productivity is not only about applying fertiliser. It is about ensuring the right nutrient is applied in the right amount, at the right place, and under the right conditions,” he said. The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Aliyu Abdullahi, represented by the Director of Agricultural Land and Climate Change Management Services, Oshadiya Olanipekun, emphasised soil data, testing and crop-specific fertiliser recommendations as important tools for improving farmers’ outcomes. Also speaking, Prof. Jibrin Mohammed Jibrin, Visiting Scientist with the Regional Hub and Professor of Soil Science at Bayero University, Kano, described soil information as fundamental to food production. Jibrin also called for better coordination among agricultural stakeholders, warning that fragmented interventions could undermine efforts to improve soil health. “The basis of food production and food security is the soil. You need healthy soil to produce well and feed the nation with nutritious food. To do that, you need soil intelligence. “Too many initiatives have been implemented in silos. Real progress will come when stakeholders align, collaborate and follow through on agreed actions,” he said. Senior Agronomist at the Regional Hub, Dr. Bello Shehu, said improving phosphorus management was not about applying more fertiliser but understanding the nutrient requirements of different soils and crops. item.title: Ogun indigenes reaffirm support for Adebutu ahead of 2027
item.description: …PDP candidate’s supporters pledge grassroots mobilisation for ‘Ogun for Ogun’ agenda By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Indigenes of Ogun State have reaffirmed their support for the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, pledging grassroots mobilisation for their ambition ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The pledge was made during ward-to-ward engagements by the candidates across local government areas of the state, where residents expressed concerns about poor infrastructure, unemployment, inadequate agricultural support and the need for improved access to modern farming equipment. The campaign tour is also aimed at presenting the candidates’ seven-point development agenda, tagged ITURA DE, to the electorate. At the ward meetings, community leaders, market women, farmers and youths turned out to receive the candidates and discuss their expectations from the next administration. Several stakeholders pledged support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ initiative, arguing that the state’s leadership should reflect the interests, heritage and aspirations of its indigenes. At Alagada Ward in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area, a market leader, Mrs Folasade Ogunye, said her support for the movement was informed by the belief that indigenous leadership would better understand the challenges confronting grassroots communities. She lamented the poor condition of roads leading to markets and the limited employment opportunities available to young people, pledging to mobilise women for door-to-door campaigns. “We, the women of Obafemi Owode, have suffered neglect. Our roads to the markets are bad, and our children need jobs. We want someone who grew up here, who knows our language and understands our struggles,” she said. At Alapakooni community, also in Obafemi Owode, some residents said to be former members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) publicly renounced their membership of the party. The defectors reportedly set bunches of APC brooms ablaze to symbolise their departure, citing dissatisfaction with the party’s political leadership and questions surrounding the identity of its governorship candidate. A community youth coordinator, Tunde Akinola, said their decision to align with Adebutu was motivated by their desire for leadership they could identify with and hold accountable. He said the group wanted to support a candidate who understood the state’s challenges and could deliver on his promises. Similarly, a community stakeholder and farmer at Onidunu Ward, Deji Bamidele, said farmers in the area wanted a government that would prioritise agricultural development through mechanisation and improved access to farming inputs. He said a farmers’ cooperative with more than 300 members had pledged support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ initiative, following Adebutu’s presentation of his agricultural plans under the ITURA DE agenda. item.title: Inter End Champions League Slump With 3-0 Win Over Feyenoord
item.description: Inter Milan got their stuttering Champions League campaign back on track with a comfortable 3-0 win Tuesday against Dutch giants Feyenoord, helped by a superb first-half strike from German defender Yann Bisseck. The three-time champions of Europe had lost their first two group games, but had far too much quality for a disappointing Feyenoord, who had little answer to Inter’s pace and attacking ability. On a clear and crisp evening in Rotterdam, the visitors quickly silenced the ever raucous crowd in De Kuip, piling on sustained pressure that paid dividends as early as the eighth minute. Bisseck was given too much space on the edge of the box, allowed to turn and drill a sumptuous curling left-footed shot low past the diving Tjark Ernst in the Feyenoord goal. Feyenoord struggled to break out of the Inter Milan high press and the Serie A champions dominated possession and territory for much of the first quarter. The home fans had to wait for half an hour before their side produced their first effort of note, a clever one-two playing in Anis Hadj Moussa, who saw his shot blocked. And Inter doubled their advantage shortly afterwards. Feyenoord’s Dutch midfielder #10 Luciano Valente (R) reacts at the end of the the UEFA Champions League, league phase, Matchday 4, football match between Feyenoord and Inter Milan at De Kuip Stadium in Rotterdam on November 3, 2026. (Photo by JOHN THYS / AFP) England international Djed Spence found himself in acres of space on the right hand side. His shot looped up off a defender, allowing Pio Esposito to bundle in with his head from short range. The beginning of the second half brought more misery for Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s men, as Feyenoord’s defence backed off and invited an advancing Piotr Zielinski to shoot. The Polish international midfielder gratefully accepted the invitation, firing home an unstoppable drive off the post on 54 minutes. With the game effectively over as a contest, Inter boss Cristian Chivu rang the changes, bringing off star striker Marcus Thuram. Halfway through the second half, fireworks launched from outside the stadium landed on the pitch and roof, causing a short interruption. And the match itself rather fizzled out, as Inter cruised and Feyenoord failed to find any spark to penetrate the Italian defences. The win saw Inter climb to a more respectable place in the middle of the Champions League table while Feyenoord’s solitary victory leaves them adrift of the knock-out phase. Feyenoord’s next Champions League encounter is a home tie against Porto, while Inter Milan welcome Stuttgart. item.title: Raphinha, Yamal Fire Barcelona To Champions League Win Over Villa
item.description: Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side’s perfect start to the competition. Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace. Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth. Unai Emery’s Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca’s greater ability in the final third. The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world. Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to. The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute. Barcelona’s Spanish forward #10 Lamine Yamal (R) and Barcelona’s English forward #17 Anthony Gordon fight for the ball with Aston Villa’s Dutch defender #22 Ian Maatsen (L) and Aston Villa’s Swedish defender #03 Victor Lindelof during the UEFA Champions League 1st round day 4 football match between FC Barcelona and Aston Villa at Camp Nou Stadium in Barcelona on November 3, 2026. (Photo by MANAURE QUINTERO / AFP) The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes’s effort. Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia was quick off his line to beat Nicolas Jackson to a dangerous through-ball. Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca’s pressing. Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end. Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner. Cancelo powered a strike narrowly over before setting up Raphinha for Barcelona’s third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot. The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal of the season across all competitions. Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games. item.title: Atiku Alleges Plot To Disrupt ADC Campaign In Sokoto, Vows Resistance
item.description: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of working to frustrate the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign in the state, alleging that protesters were being mobilised to disrupt the party’s planned rally. Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, made the allegations at a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, claiming that the party had been denied access to public facilities and logistical support ahead of the rally. He said the restrictions were part of a deliberate effort to place the opposition at a disadvantage and undermine the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. “These are not harmless administrative delays. They are deliberate attempts to deny the ADC a level playing field,” he said. ﻿ Atiku also alleged that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew and prevent the rally from taking place. He identified an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road as one of the locations where the protesters were allegedly gathered. “We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko road. “Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout. These mobilised protesters are causing gridlock. “Commuters are being threatened and, in some cases, beaten. Some of the protesters have moved away from the roundabout to find shade,” he said. The former Vice President accused security personnel allegedly involved in the operation of abandoning their professional duties for political interests. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform. Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis,” he said. He asked the officers involved to end the alleged mobilisation and discharge their duties without political bias. Turning to the wider political climate, Atiku accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of attempting to weaken opposition parties by drawing their members into the ruling APC. He described the strategy as one of political absorption and intimidation, warning that its ultimate objective was to leave Nigeria with little meaningful opposition. “The aim is to reduce Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name,” he said. Atiku also faulted the Federal Government’s handling of the economy, pointing to the rising prices of food, transport, fuel and electricity as evidence of the pressure on households. He said the ADC would pursue policies aimed at expanding local production, increasing food supply, generating employment and lowering the cost of doing business if elected in 2027. Among his proposals is a targeted production subsidy linked to fuel refined in Nigeria. He said the measure would ease the burden on consumers while supporting domestic industry. item.title: Seen And Heard At The US Midterm Elections
item.description: Reporters, photographers and video journalists are deployed by AFP across the United States to document the 2026 midterm elections as Americans head to the polls. Here is a round-up of interviews on Tuesday at polling stations where voters agreed to share their thoughts about what was on their minds and motivating their choices. Hopeful Democrats With polling data suggesting the Democratic Party is on track to capture a majority in the House of Representatives and perhaps even in the Senate, many left-leaning voters said they were hopeful about the results. “Two years ago was a really devastating outcome for me,” Emma Mondadori, a 39-year-old who works in philanthropy, told AFP in Brooklyn, New York, referring to President Donald Trump’s election. “I’ve been really looking forward to this day where we get to have a say again in the future of our country… I’m cautiously hopeful, optimistic.” AUSTIN, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 03: Voters wait in line to cast their ballots at the polling place at the Baker Center on November 03, 2026 in Austin, Texas. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by CHIP SOMODEVILLA / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) The cost of living With gasoline prices up by a third since last year and diesel nearly double — not to mention sharp food price inflation — everyday spending was on many people’s minds. “It’s about the cost of living, gas prices, those kind of things. It needs to change for the everyday person, and I’m an everyday person,” Donta Comer, a 38-year-old project manager in Atlanta, Georgia, told AFP. Tom, a 27-year-old businessman at the same polling station who declined to give his surname, agreed. “Everyone, at least in my generation, is a little frustrated with the affordability crisis and gas prices and what’s going on abroad,” added the non-partisan voter. Leadership referendum Mid-term elections are typically seen as a form of referendum on the sitting president. And few leaders have polarized public opinion as strongly as Donald Trump. “I’m independent but I voted Democrat, I just wanted to go back into the culture of decency, integrity, honesty, and the rest follows,” Yan Cardineau, 59, told AFP in Austin, Texas. “If we lose that, it doesn’t matter how much money you make.” Atlantans head to the polls to vote on Election Day at Park Tavern on November 3, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Megan Varner/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Megan Varner / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) Estrella Roque, a 69-year-old voter of Cuban origin, told AFP in Miami she had voted Republican. “What I like about the Republicans is that they can fix the country,” she explained in Spanish. “Donald Trump hasn’t been given time to show who he really is.” Immigration In his final pitch to voters, Trump has stressed his success in reducing immigration and stopping crossings along the southern border with Mexico.
